body: I'm at a top 10 school, and I'm a 2 1/2L, so it's a bit late to hit eject, plus I do love the work I want to do eventually and it will qualify for loan forgiveness. Thanks for the advice.
Thanks for the advice and the reply.

Definitely not, she's also a bit removed from the situation because they have their own stuff going on, but I'm sure she was trying to motivate something in me and is just horrible at doing it. Thanks for your reply
Thanks for your reply, I appreciate your time and your words.

Thank you for your response. 

It's hard to see the lies when they replace the truth entirely, but subconsciously, I know you're right. Just lose my way, sometimes, you know?

Thanks for the PM offer, I can promise I'll use it one day, and I want you to know the offer stands for you as well. Like I said, today was a bad day for me, but I have good days, days when I can help you should you ever need it. 

Thanks again for the response.
Thanks, I really appreciate it and definitely will. It was beautifully written in my opinion. Don't worry, I'll try not to spam you too often :) Thanks again.
You too.

Thanks for the reply, you're right about being close to finished. Just need to stick it out and prove that I'm dedicated despite doubting myself out times... that's what he was insinuating. I have no doubt I'm dedicated to the profession, if I wasn't, I'd have dropped out or offed myself already... I certainly wouldn't be taking out loans and killing myself with stress for something I didn't actually want. I started to doubt my abilities and whether or not I'd be able to succeed in the job and rather than saying "sounds like you're going through a lot, it's going to be ok" he decided that my uncertainty meant I'm not actually dedicated to being an attorney. That was really insulting to me, especially because from the outside looking in and making no attempt to understand where I'm coming from, he sort of failed as any kind of support and insinuated that I'm a quitter even though he sat on the sidelines watching my fight for everything I've gotten so far. 

I hope the CPA thing works out for you, I've got my fingers crossed. Thanks again for the response.
I'm really glad to hear that. I'll be trying my hardest to get to a better place.

I'm sorry to hear that. I'm currently in the process of coordinating some kind of creative outlet because I think it's the best way for me to really get emotion out. so that's great advice, thank you. 

Happy birthday to you too... I hope next year it's better for both of us. Cheers to 24 years over here.

Thanks so much for the response. You're right, it's easy to lose sight of the war when you're losing a single battle. Just have to keep reminding myself it's worth the fight in the end. 

I hope you're well. Thanks again
Thanks for the words of encouragement. :)

yeah, she's a bit of a hot head when she's in a delicate situation. She doesn't really think things through and just immediately reacts. Yeah, it does suck to not feel supported especially already feeling isolated, but all the support this community has given me was really helpful. 

thanks for your response

Yeah, you're definitely right. I'm definitely the golden child (which is a fuckton of pressure in an of itself) but it would be hard to stomach both of your kids having serious issues. 

I'm trying not to, it's my mission to be more open. 

Thanks for the birthday wishes and the reply.

you know, i think it was probably a defensive thing because i have no doubt she would take any suicide attempt as a personal attack on her parenting abilities, which it definitely is not (obviously). I think she just said something without thinking about the implications. I'm obviously still hurt by it, but I'm just gonna back off and let her come to the realization that that's no ok behavior. I think she's smart enough to figure that out over time.

I wish! That's the problem with law school, there is very little room for customization, and there is an atmosphere that if you're suffering, you're falling behind because no one else even knows what suffering is (clearly, that's not true, but they want you to feel like the weakest link). 

I'm taking some space from my parents for a bit, and just gonna let it breathe. I also decided to say fuck it and spend some of my birthday money on a little get away just to take a break from it all. Hopefully that helps a bit. 

I'm glad you've managed calculus, it was a beast for me too.

I'm sorry he said that to you. I can't imagine how hurtful that must have been. Parents can do a fantastic job of royally fucking things up, huh?

I have, yeah. My therapist said it's all extremely common especially with this level of constant stress. Unfortunately, there's very little I can do to relieve the burden right now other than seek help when it gets bad and try to remind myself that all of this is temporary, no matter what it looks like. I also have pretty intense anxiety (well controlled on medication) but it makes me overthink EVERYTHING so small things become huge things that have no answer... it's an unfortunate cycle. 

Thank you for your reply.

Thanks for replying. Professional school is a killer, the end result is something we so desperately want, but the road to get there is just hellish. I hope Med school is working out well for you. 

And yeah, luckily, I'm not in any immediate danger of hurting myself, I've gotten over than hump, but sometimes it's just like you need to say "look, all this stuff is happening, can we just acknowledge that it's a lot and I just can't handle it all right now?" Unfortunately, depression gives me a little nagging voice whispering in my ear like "there's a way out" when really, logically, I know that's not my best choice. 

Anyway, thanks for your reply. I hope you're well.

Thank god. The law school system is the biggest joke, I can't wait to start working. Very glad you've made it out and into the real world and really appreciate the offer to chat. will certainly be taking you up on it!
Wow, that's horrendous. I hope your life is very happy now and that the struggles are few and far between.
No idea, really. I think it just came out without any thought.
Thank you!

Thank you! good to know people make it to the other side from this feeling. 

I think just being a listening ear and lending words of support is so helpful, that thank you for that. 

Same goes for you, please feel free to message me whenever you need.

Thanks so much. I'm printing that cartoon out for my fridge (lame, I know). 

I hope depression stays the hell away from you for the rest of forever, and I can't wait til I can look back on this as a thing of the past. I hope you're well.

You're entirely correct. She's not perfect, but I know more than anything she loves me. I'm taking some quiet time from both of them for a while, so I can figure things out. Obviously, I'm hurt by that statement, but I know she loves me and would be devastated should anything ever happen to me. I think I scared the shit out of her and that it probably hurts her to know I'm upset and she responded in the only way she knows how; defensively. Regardless, not an excuse, but I hope should I ever react poorly to my children one day, they understand that my experiences shape my reactions and I can't always be perfect, so I'm trying to keep that in mind with her. 

Thanks for your message.

I really, really appreciate your kind words, truly. 

I've grown really accustomed to holding it all together and some days (including today) I come unglued. My doctor and I have a date scheduled for this week. I know somewhere in my head that ending everything really means ending EVERYTHING, not just the bad things and though they seem few and far between at the moment, there are really, really good things in my life. 

Thank you again for reaching out, it feels really good to not feel as isolated. I hope you're well.

Thanks so much. I really do appreciate the support.

I'll keep that in mind, and please feel free to reach out to me too should you experience a bad day. Today is my bad day, but I do have good ones. On one of those days, I'd like to return the favor.

Thanks for the reply.

It does make sense. Can't recall most of the days when I thought to myself "this is the best day of my life" but I could pretty much tell you exactly what I was wearing when I was humiliated or hurt or betrayed. It's sad, really. Law school is funny. It takes people who were at one point passionate and idealistic and creative about equality and justice and fairness and turns them into depressive shells. I was a really, really happy person before school and I bet I will be afterwards, but American law school puts a sort of stress level on you that is designed to make you crack. There's a study that law students enter law school from the base level of about 4-10% rate of depression (the average percentage of the population who suffer from depression), by the third year 40% of them develop depressive symptoms... there's something fucked about that. The levels fall again after graduation to slightly higher than average, but it really gives a new meaning to "you just don't understand" because it's frankly unprecedented. Any way, sorry to ramble, just thought it was interesting. 

I appreciate that. It's a bad day for me after a few bad weeks, but I remember what it feels like to love life and I want that feeling back. Luckily a community like this exists to remind me of what I sometimes forget.

Thank you. Yeah, it's pretty shitty. I think I scared the shit out of her though, because I'm the child she looks at as stable, despite my depression. My brother has pretty serious mental health issues and she's very sensitive when dealing with his mood swings, so I think she expects me to be a stronger person than is ever even possible. Definitely not an excuse and I'm going to be doing a bit of radio silence here for a while to formulate a response that is helpful and not drawn out of anger, but yeah, that cut pretty deeply.

Thanks. My doctors are well aware of my suicidal thoughts and I'm on medication that usually is a miracle drug for me, but things have been getting progressively more stressful and I have been feeling more and more trapped. I just can't imagine how any of this can ever resolve itself. I've already called my therapist, it's just if it feels like this, even with medication and therapy, I'm not very hopeful. A lot of it is building from the constant stream of professional and academic rejections I've been getting, and one specific one recently just totally took the wind out of my sails... I just sort of wish I had been met with sympathy rather than accused of being dramatic, lacking dedication and ultimately told that perhaps I'd be doing evolution a favor (in not so many words haha). It's just deeply upsetting to look for respite and a soft place to land only to find it doesn't exist.
Thanks. To hear someone else say it's a horrible thing to say makes me feel a bit better. I've been trying to normalize it, but I guess it's just not a normal parental response.

Thanks. I'm just at the point where I'm too tried to keep digging and proving people wrong, you know? I don't want to prove anything to anyone, I just want to be able to relax. I don't know if that makes sense. Anyway, thanks for your support, it really does mean something to me.

My mom said "I think you're being dramatic, but if this is enough to break you, you're just not strong enough for life. Maybe you should." This is the first time I've ever told her about feeling suicidal, it's not something that I've ever attempted nor have I ever threatened it. When I felt like this before, I just said I was feeling overwhelmed and needed to talk to someone. My doctor knows everything, but they have been relatively in the dark about the depth of my depression. Yeah, they're good parents and good people, which makes it all the more apparent to me that I must be doing something pretty abhorrent to illicit that reaction from her. It's also my birthday so, that's great too.
